chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When you pray facing a direction other than the Qiblah, and it becomes clear to you before morning that you prayed facing a direction other than the Qiblah, then repeat your prayer.

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The Qiblah, the direction of prayer towards the Kaaba in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I realize I prayed facing the wrong direction before morning?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for unintentional misdirection during prayer, specifying that re-prayer is required only if the error is discovered before dawn (subh). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus on the necessity of facing the Qiblah as a condition for the validity of Salah, distinguishing between minor deviations and complete misalignment. It underscores the importance of vigilance in ritual practice while providing leniency for those who realize their mistake within a specific timeframe.
